dua.ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا، وَرِزْقًا طَيِّبًا، وَعَمَلًا مُتَقَبَّلًا
dua.tr: Allahumma inni as'aluka 'ilman nafi'an, wa rizqan tayyiban, wa 'amalan mutaqabbalan
dua.en: O Allah, I ask You for knowledge that benefits, provision that is good and pure, and deeds that are accepted.
dua.note: The Prophet ﷺ would say this after the Fajr prayer. A beautiful way to begin each working day.

items.title: Seek forgiveness (istighfar)
items.text: Nuh told his people that asking Allah's forgiveness brings rain, wealth, children and gardens. Make it a daily habit.

items.title: Thank Allah for what you have
items.text: Allah promises more to those who are grateful. Name three blessings out loud or in your journal.

items.title: Guard your taqwa
items.text: Whoever is mindful of Allah, He makes a way out for them and provides from where they never expected.

items.title: Work hard, then rely on Allah
items.text: Birds leave their nests hungry in the morning and return full. Do your part and trust Him with the outcome.

items.title: A few rak'ahs of tahajjud
items.text: The best prayer after the obligatory ones is the night prayer. Even two short rak'ahs before Fajr count.

items.title: Keep family ties
items.text: Whoever wants their provision widened and life extended should keep in touch with relatives. A call or message is a start.

items.title: Give some charity
items.text: Charity never decreases wealth. Even a small coin or a kind act counts as sadaqah today.

items.title: Start work early in the morning
items.text: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for blessing in his ummah's early mornings. Use the fresh hours after Fajr for your most important task.

items.title: Be honest in every deal
items.text: When buyer and seller are truthful and clear, their deal is blessed; hiding faults wipes the blessing away.

items.title: Plan or save for Hajj & Umrah
items.text: Following Hajj with Umrah removes poverty and sins as a furnace removes impurity. Set aside a little towards it.

items.title: Spend on your family with good intention
items.text: Money spent on your family carries great reward when done for Allah's sake. Even a meal you share is charity.

items.title: Pray each salah on time
items.text: Prayer at its proper time is among the deeds Allah loves most. Let your work fit around salah, not the other way round.

items.title: Morning & evening adhkar
items.text: Remember Allah often and glorify Him morning and evening. A few minutes that set the tone for the whole day.

items.title: Read some Quran
items.text: Those who recite the Book and pray hope for a trade that will never fail. One page a day adds up.

items.title: One small deed, done consistently
items.text: The deeds most loved by Allah are the regular ones, even if small. Pick one and keep it going today.

items.title: Use your time with purpose
items.text: Each of us will be asked how we spent our life. Before scrolling, ask: is this how I want to spend it?

items.title: Sleep soon after Isha
items.text: The Prophet ﷺ disliked chatting late after Isha. An early night makes Fajr and the blessed morning easier.

items.title: Say salam when entering home
items.text: Greet your household with a greeting of peace from Allah, blessed and good, even if the house seems empty.

items.title: Mention Allah entering and eating
items.text: When Allah is remembered on entering and at meals, Shaytan finds no place to stay or eat in your home.

items.title: Recite Surah al-Baqarah at home
items.text: Shaytan flees from a house in which Surah al-Baqarah is recited. Read or play part of it today.

items.title: Share a meal together
items.text: Food for one is enough for two, and food for two is enough for four. Sharing multiplies what you have.

items.title: Be at your best with your family
items.text: The best of you are those who are best to their families. Help with a chore, as the Prophet ﷺ did at home.

items.title: Pray a voluntary prayer at home
items.text: Pray some of your prayers in your houses and do not turn them into graves. It fills the home with light.

items.title: Eat in moderation
items.text: A third for food, a third for drink, a third for air. Stop before you feel full.

items.title: Don't waste food
items.text: Finish what is on your plate and lick your fingers, for you do not know which part holds the blessing.

items.title: Move your body
items.text: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak, though there is good in both. A walk counts.

items.title: Value health and free time
items.text: Many people lose out on two blessings: health and free time. Use today's energy for something good.

items.title: Use the siwak / brush your teeth
items.text: The Prophet ﷺ was so keen on siwak that he would have commanded it before every prayer if not for hardship.

items.title: Sleep with wudu on your right side
items.text: Make wudu before bed, lie on your right side and say the bedtime dua. Rest becomes worship.
